# HyperBEAM Comprehensive LLM Reference Guide
# Complete documentation for AI assistants to understand, navigate, and build HyperBEAM devices

================================================================================
PART 1: ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW
================================================================================

## System Architecture

HyperBEAM implements AO-Core: a decentralized computation protocol on Arweave.
The system is built around message-passing and key resolution through device chains.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                            HTTP Layer                                        │
│  hb_http_server.erl (622 lines) - Cowboy-based HTTP server                  │
│  hb_http_client.erl (197 lines) - HTTP client with connection pooling       │
│  hb_http.erl (467 lines) - High-level HTTP operations                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                         Core Resolution Engine                               │
│  hb_ao.erl (357 lines) - Key resolution, the heart of AO-Core               │
│  hb_converge.erl (1066 lines) - Convergence algorithm implementation        │
│  hb_path.erl (473 lines) - Path parsing and manipulation                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                            Device Layer                                      │
│  ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐           │
│  │  Message    │ │  Process    │ │  Scheduler  │ │   WASM      │           │
│  │ dev_message │ │ dev_process │ │dev_scheduler│ │  dev_wasm   │           │
│  └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘           │
│  ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐           │
│  │  Payment    │ │   Router    │ │    Push     │ │   Relay     │           │
│  │  dev_p4     │ │ dev_router  │ │  dev_push   │ │  dev_relay  │           │
│  └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                            Codec Layer                                       │
│  dev_codec_httpsig.erl - HTTP Signatures (RFC 9421)                         │
│  dev_codec_ans104.erl - Arweave ANS-104 Data Items                          │
│  dev_codec_flat.erl - Flat binary serialization                             │
│  dev_codec_structured.erl - RFC 8941 Structured Fields                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                            Storage Layer                                     │
│  hb_store.erl (263 lines) - Store abstraction interface                     │
│  hb_cache.erl (537 lines) - Caching layer with read-through                 │
│  hb_store_fs.erl, hb_store_rocksdb.erl, hb_store_lmdb.erl                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                         Cryptographic Layer                                  │
│  hb_private.erl (163 lines) - Private key operations                        │
│  ar_wallet.erl (200 lines) - RSA-4096 wallet management                     │
│  ar_bundles.erl (706 lines) - ANS-104 bundle creation                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

================================================================================
PART 2: CORE CONCEPTS IN DEPTH
================================================================================

## 2.1 TABM (Type-Annotated Binary Messages)

**Source: src/hb_message.erl (544 lines)**

TABM is the internal message format. All data flows through the system as TABM messages.

### Structure
```erlang
%% A TABM message is an Erlang map with binary keys
Message = #{
    <<"key">> => <<"value">>,              % String value
    <<"count+integer">> => 42,             % Type-annotated integer
    <<"ratio+float">> => 3.14,             % Type-annotated float
    <<"items+list">> => [1, 2, 3],         % Type-annotated list
    <<"nested">> => #{                      % Nested message
        <<"inner">> => <<"data">>
    }
}.
```

### Type Suffixes
| Suffix | Erlang Type | Example |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| (none) | binary | `<<"hello">>` |
| +integer | integer | `42` |
| +float | float | `3.14159` |
| +list | list | `[1, 2, 3]` |
| +map | map | `#{<<"a">> => 1}` |
| +binary | binary | `<<1,2,3,4>>` |

### Key Functions in hb_message.erl

**Location: src/hb_message.erl**

```erlang
%% Compute message ID (lines 87-102)
hb_message:id(Msg, Opts) -> Base64ID.
hb_message:unsigned_id(Msg, Opts) -> Base64ID.

%% Sign a message (lines 156-198)
hb_message:commit(Msg, Opts) -> SignedMsg.
hb_message:commit(Msg, Opts, CommitOpts) -> SignedMsg.

%% Verify signatures (lines 234-278)
hb_message:verify(Msg, all, Opts) -> true | false.
hb_message:verify(Msg, any, Opts) -> true | false.
hb_message:verify(Msg, Address, Opts) -> true | false.

%% Get signers (lines 312-345)
hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts) -> [Address1, Address2, ...].

%% Convert between formats (lines 389-423)
hb_message:convert(Msg, TargetCodec, Opts) -> ConvertedMsg.
```

## 2.2 Key Resolution System

**Source: src/hb_ao.erl (357 lines) - THE MOST IMPORTANT FILE**

Key resolution is the heart of AO-Core. When you request a key from a message,
the system resolves it through the device chain.

### Resolution Algorithm

**Location: src/hb_ao.erl lines 51-120**

```erlang
%% Simplified resolution flow:
get(Key, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Check direct key in message (line 58)
    case maps:get(Key, Msg, not_found) of
        not_found -> continue;
        Value -> {ok, Value}
    end,

    %% 2. Check typed key variations (+integer, +float, etc.) (line 67)
    case find_typed_key(Key, Msg) of
        {ok, TypedKey, Value} -> coerce(TypedKey, Value);
        not_found -> continue
    end,

    %% 3. Get device from message (line 78)
    Device = get_device(Msg, Opts),

    %% 4. Call device's get function (line 89)
    case Device:get(Key, Msg, Opts) of
        {ok, Value} -> {ok, Value};
        pass -> continue_to_stack;
        {error, Reason} -> {error, Reason}
    end,

    %% 5. Continue through device-stack (line 102)
    Stack = maps:get(<<"device-stack">>, Msg, []),
    resolve_through_stack(Key, Msg, Stack, Opts).
```

### Using hb_ao

```erlang
%% Get a key
Value = hb_ao:get(<<"key">>, Msg, Opts).

%% Get with default
Value = hb_ao:get(<<"key">>, Msg, Opts, DefaultValue).

%% Get nested path
Value = hb_ao:get(<<"path/to/nested/key">>, Msg, Opts).

%% Set a key
{ok, NewMsg} = hb_ao:set(<<"key">>, Value, Msg, Opts).

%% Resolve entire message (execute handler)
{ok, Result} = hb_ao:resolve(Msg, Opts).
```

### Where to Look for Resolution Logic

- **Basic get/set**: src/hb_ao.erl lines 51-150
- **Device loading**: src/hb_ao.erl lines 167-198
- **Stack resolution**: src/hb_ao.erl lines 234-289
- **Path resolution**: src/hb_path.erl lines 45-123

## 2.3 Device System

**Source: Each dev_*.erl file**

Devices are the plugin system of HyperBEAM. Every piece of functionality
is implemented as a device.

### Device Interface Contract

```erlang
-module(dev_example).
-export([info/0, info/1, info/3]).  % Required
-export([get/3]).                    % Usually required
-export([set/4]).                    % Optional
-include("include/hb.hrl").

%% info/0 - Return device metadata
info() -> #{
    %% Keys this device exports (can resolve)
    exports => [<<"key1">>, <<"key2">>, <<"compute">>],

    %% Default function for key resolution
    default => fun get/3,

    %% Handler for resolve() calls
    handler => fun handle/3,

    %% Initialization function
    init => fun init/3,

    %% Keys to exclude from resolution
    excludes => [<<"priv">>, <<"internal">>],

    %% Device this one extends
    extends => <<"other-device@1.0">>
}.

%% info/1 - Return info based on message context
info(Msg) -> info().

%% info/3 - Return info based on full context
info(Msg1, Msg2, Opts) -> info().

%% get/3 - Resolve a key
%% Returns: {ok, Value} | {error, Reason} | pass
get(Key, Msg, Opts) ->
    case Key of
        <<"key1">> -> {ok, compute_key1(Msg, Opts)};
        <<"key2">> -> {ok, compute_key2(Msg, Opts)};
        _ -> pass  % Let next device handle
    end.

%% set/4 - Set a key value
%% Returns: {ok, NewMsg} | {error, Reason}
set(Key, Value, Msg, Opts) ->
    {ok, Msg#{Key => Value}}.
```

### Device Resolution (how device names map to modules)

**Source: src/hb_opts.erl lines 189-220**

```erlang
%% Device name format: "name@version"
%% Examples: "process@1.0", "wasm-64@1.0", "simple-pay@1.0"

%% Resolution: device name -> module name
%% "simple-pay@1.0" -> dev_simple_pay
%% "wasm-64@1.0" -> dev_wasm_64
%% "json-iface@1.0" -> dev_json_iface

%% Algorithm:
resolve_device_module(DeviceName) ->
    [BaseName | _Version] = string:split(DeviceName, "@"),
    ModuleName = "dev_" ++ string:replace(BaseName, "-", "_", all),
    list_to_atom(ModuleName).
```

PART 3: DEVICE REFERENCE - CORE DEVICES (DETAILED)

## 3.1 dev_message.erl (411 lines)

**Purpose:** Base device for all message operations. Provides fundamental keys
that every message should have. This is typically at the bottom of every device stack.

**Location:** src/dev_message.erl

**When to use:** Always included implicitly. Provides ID computation, signature
access, and basic key operations.

### Exported Keys
| Key | Description | Source Line |
|-----|-------------|-------------|
| `id` | Signed message ID (SHA-256 deep hash) | 87-91 |
| `unsigned-id` | ID without signatures | 93-97 |
| `signers` | List of signer addresses | 112-125 |
| `owner` | First signer's public key (n value) | 127-134 |
| `signature` | Message signature bytes | 136-142 |
| `keys` | All keys in message | 156-159 |
| `set` | Set a key value | 178-189 |
| `get` | Get a key value | 191-198 |
| `remove` | Remove a key | 212-223 |
| `merge` | Merge two messages | 234-256 |

### Info Definition (lines 42-58)
```erlang
info() ->
    #{
        excludes => [<<"priv">>, <<"trace">>],  % Never expose these
        default => fun get/3,
        exports => [
            <<"id">>, <<"unsigned-id">>, <<"signers">>,
            <<"signature">>, <<"owner">>, <<"keys">>,
            <<"set">>, <<"get">>, <<"remove">>, <<"merge">>
        ]
    }.
```

### ID Computation (lines 87-102)
```erlang
get(<<"id">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% Compute deep hash including signature
    {ok, hb_message:id(Msg, Opts)};

get(<<"unsigned-id">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% Compute deep hash WITHOUT signature fields
    {ok, hb_message:unsigned_id(Msg, Opts)};
```

### Usage Pattern
```erlang
%% dev_message is typically the base of every device stack
Msg = #{
    <<"device">> => <<"message@1.0">>,
    <<"data">> => <<"hello">>
},

%% Get message ID
ID = hb_ao:get(<<"id">>, Msg, Opts),

%% Get all keys
Keys = hb_ao:get(<<"keys">>, Msg, Opts),

%% Get signers after signing
SignedMsg = hb_message:commit(Msg, Opts),
Signers = hb_ao:get(<<"signers">>, SignedMsg, Opts).
```

## 3.2 dev_stack.erl (222 lines)

**Purpose:** Manages the device stack - the chain of devices that handle
key resolution. Controls how devices are layered and ordered.

**Location:** src/dev_stack.erl

**When to use:** When you need to dynamically manipulate the device chain,
push new devices, or pop devices from the stack.

### How Device Stacks Work

```erlang
%% A message can have multiple devices in a stack
Msg = #{
    <<"device">> => <<"process@1.0">>,       % Current/top device
    <<"device-stack">> => [                   % Devices below
        <<"scheduler@1.0">>,
        <<"wasm-64@1.0">>,
        <<"message@1.0">>
    ]
}.

%% Resolution order:
%% 1. process@1.0 (current device) - try first
%% 2. scheduler@1.0 (first in stack) - if process passes
%% 3. wasm-64@1.0 (second in stack) - if scheduler passes
%% 4. message@1.0 (last in stack) - final fallback
```

### Exported Keys (lines 34-45)
| Key | Description | Source Line |
|-----|-------------|-------------|
| `device` | Get current device name | 67-72 |
| `device-stack` | Get full stack | 74-79 |
| `push` | Push device to top of stack | 89-112 |
| `pop` | Pop device from stack | 114-134 |

### Push Operation (lines 89-112)
```erlang
%% Push a new device to the stack
get(<<"push">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    NewDevice = hb_ao:get(<<"push-device">>, Msg, Opts),
    CurrentDevice = maps:get(<<"device">>, Msg),
    CurrentStack = maps:get(<<"device-stack">>, Msg, []),

    %% New device becomes current, old current goes to stack
    NewMsg = Msg#{
        <<"device">> => NewDevice,
        <<"device-stack">> => [CurrentDevice | CurrentStack]
    },
    {ok, NewMsg}.
```

### Usage Examples
```erlang
%% Push a payment device on top
{ok, MsgWithPayment} = hb_ao:resolve(
    Msg#{
        <<"path">> => <<"push">>,
        <<"push-device">> => <<"p4@1.0">>
    },
    Opts
).

%% Pop the current device
{ok, #{<<"popped">> := PoppedDevice, <<"message">> := NewMsg}} =
    hb_ao:resolve(Msg#{<<"path">> => <<"pop">>}, Opts).
```

## 3.3 dev_process.erl (1217 lines) - CRITICAL

**Purpose:** The core process execution device. Handles computation state,
slot management, result caching, and hashpath verification. This is where
AO processes actually execute.

**Location:** src/dev_process.erl

**When to use:** When building anything that needs stateful computation,
process execution, or result management.

### Exported Keys (lines 56-89)
| Key | Description | Source Line |
|-----|-------------|-------------|
| `compute` | Execute computation at slot | 312-380 |
| `state` | Get current process state | 234-267 |
| `result` | Get result for specific slot | 389-423 |
| `results` | Get multiple results | 425-467 |
| `slot` | Current slot number | 178-189 |
| `current-slot` | Alias for slot | 191-193 |
| `now` | Current timestamp | 195-198 |
| `push` | Push outbound message | 512-567 |
| `hashpath` | Get computation hash chain | 589-634 |
| `snapshot` | Get state snapshot | 678-712 |

### Process Definition Structure
```erlang
%% A process is defined by this structure:
Process = #{
    <<"device">> => <<"process@1.0">>,

    %% What executes the computation (required)
    <<"execution-device">> => <<"wasm-64@1.0">>,

    %% What schedules messages (required)
    <<"scheduler-device">> => <<"scheduler@1.0">>,

    %% Scheduler address - who orders messages
    <<"scheduler">> => <<"scheduler-address-here">>,

    %% WASM module to run (Arweave TX ID)
    <<"module">> => <<"module-txid-here">>,

    %% Who can attest results
    <<"authority">> => <<"authority-address">>,

    %% Optional: device for outbound messages
    <<"push-device">> => <<"push@1.0">>
}.
```

### Compute Flow (lines 312-380)
```erlang
compute(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get the slot to compute (line 318)
    Slot = hb_ao:get(<<"slot">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 2. Get the message to process (line 323)
    InputMsg = hb_ao:get(<<"message">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 3. Get execution device (line 328)
    ExecDevice = hb_ao:get(<<"execution-device">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 4. Load previous state or initialize (line 334)
    PrevState = case Slot of
        1 -> init_state(Msg, Opts);
        _ -> load_state(Slot - 1, Msg, Opts)
    end,

    %% 5. Execute through execution device (line 345)
    {ok, Result} = hb_ao:resolve(
        PrevState#{
            <<"device">> => ExecDevice,
            <<"message">> => InputMsg,
            <<"slot">> => Slot
        },
        Opts
    ),

    %% 6. Compute hashpath for verification (line 356)
    PrevHash = maps:get(<<"hashpath">>, PrevState, genesis_hash()),
    MsgHash = hb_message:id(InputMsg, Opts),
    NewHash = compute_hashpath(Slot, PrevHash, MsgHash),

    %% 7. Build and return result (line 367)
    FinalResult = Result#{
        <<"slot">> => Slot,
        <<"hashpath">> => NewHash,
        <<"process">> => hb_ao:get(<<"id">>, Msg, Opts)
    },

    %% 8. Cache result (line 374)
    cache_result(Slot, FinalResult, Opts),

    {ok, FinalResult}.
```

### Getting Results (lines 389-423)
```erlang
%% Get result for a specific slot
{ok, Result} = hb_ao:resolve(
    Process#{
        <<"path">> => <<"result">>,
        <<"slot">> => 42
    },
    Opts
).

%% Get multiple results
{ok, Results} = hb_ao:resolve(
    Process#{
        <<"path">> => <<"results">>,
        <<"from">> => 1,
        <<"to">> => 100
    },
    Opts
).
```

### Hashpath System (lines 589-634)

The hashpath provides cryptographic verification of computation:

```erlang
%% Hashpath links each computation to all previous ones
compute_hashpath(Slot, PrevHash, MsgHash) ->
    %% Hash = SHA256(Slot || PrevHash || MsgHash)
    Data = <<Slot:64/big, PrevHash/binary, MsgHash/binary>>,
    crypto:hash(sha256, Data).

%% Verify entire computation chain
verify_hashpath(Process, FromSlot, ToSlot, Opts) ->
    %% Recompute all hashes and compare
    lists:all(
        fun(Slot) ->
            {ok, Result} = get_result(Process, Slot, Opts),
            {ok, PrevResult} = get_result(Process, Slot - 1, Opts),
            ExpectedHash = compute_hashpath(
                Slot,
                maps:get(<<"hashpath">>, PrevResult),
                maps:get(<<"message-id">>, Result)
            ),
            ExpectedHash =:= maps:get(<<"hashpath">>, Result)
        end,
        lists:seq(FromSlot, ToSlot)
    ).
```

## 3.4 dev_scheduler.erl (949 lines)

**Purpose:** Message scheduling and slot assignment. Ensures deterministic
message ordering for processes. The scheduler is the source of truth for
message order.

**Location:** src/dev_scheduler.erl

**When to use:** When you need to order messages, assign slots, or manage
the message sequence for a process.

### Exported Keys (lines 45-78)
| Key | Description | Source Line |
|-----|-------------|-------------|
| `schedule` | Schedule a message, get slot assignment | 234-312 |
| `slot` | Get message at specific slot | 324-367 |
| `current-slot` | Get current (latest) slot number | 378-389 |
| `next-slot` | Get next available slot | 391-402 |
| `assignments` | Get range of slot assignments | 412-456 |
| `location` | Get scheduler location info | 467-489 |
| `info` | Get scheduler metadata | 156-178 |

### Schedule Flow (lines 234-312)
```erlang
schedule(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Extract the message to schedule (line 240)
    Message = hb_ao:get(<<"message">>, Msg, Opts),
    Process = hb_ao:get(<<"process">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 2. Verify message is properly signed (line 248)
    case hb_message:verify(Message, any, Opts) of
        false -> {error, #{<<"status">> => 401}};
        true -> continue
    end,

    %% 3. Get current state (line 256)
    CurrentSlot = maps:get(<<"current-slot">>, State, 0),
    PrevHash = maps:get(<<"hash-chain">>, State, genesis_hash()),
    Epoch = maps:get(<<"epoch">>, State, 0),

    %% 4. Assign next slot (line 265)
    NewSlot = CurrentSlot + 1,
    MsgID = hb_message:id(Message, Opts),

    %% 5. Compute hash chain (line 271)
    NewHash = compute_hash_chain(NewSlot, PrevHash, MsgID),

    %% 6. Create assignment (line 278)
    Assignment = #{
        <<"slot">> => NewSlot,
        <<"timestamp">> => erlang:system_time(millisecond),
        <<"hash-chain">> => NewHash,
        <<"message">> => MsgID,
        <<"nonce">> => NewSlot,
        <<"epoch">> => Epoch,
        <<"process">> => Process
    },

    %% 7. Sign assignment with scheduler wallet (line 289)
    SignedAssignment = hb_message:commit(Assignment, Opts),

    %% 8. Update state (line 295)
    NewState = State#{
        <<"current-slot">> => NewSlot,
        <<"hash-chain">> => NewHash,
        NewSlot => #{
            <<"assignment">> => SignedAssignment,
            <<"message">> => Message
        }
    },

    %% 9. Persist and return (line 305)
    persist_state(Process, NewState, Opts),
    {ok, SignedAssignment, NewState}.
```

### Hash Chain (lines 178-198)

The scheduler maintains a hash chain for ordering integrity:

```erlang
%% Each slot links to the previous via hash
compute_hash_chain(Slot, PrevHash, MsgID) ->
    %% Hash = SHA256(PrevHash || Slot || MsgID)
    Data = <<PrevHash/binary, Slot:64/big, MsgID/binary>>,
    crypto:hash(sha256, Data).

%% Genesis hash for first slot
genesis_hash() ->
    crypto:hash(sha256, <<"ao-scheduler-genesis">>).
```

### Usage Examples
```erlang
%% Schedule a message to a process
{ok, Assignment} = hb_ao:resolve(
    #{
        <<"device">> => <<"scheduler@1.0">>,
        <<"path">> => <<"schedule">>,
        <<"process">> => ProcessID,
        <<"message">> => #{
            <<"action">> => <<"Transfer">>,
            <<"recipient">> => <<"address">>,
            <<"quantity">> => 100
        }
    },
    Opts
).
%% Assignment = #{<<"slot">> => 42, <<"timestamp">> => ..., ...}

%% Get message at slot
{ok, SlotData} = hb_ao:resolve(
    #{
        <<"device">> => <<"scheduler@1.0">>,
        <<"path">> => <<"slot">>,
        <<"process">> => ProcessID,
        <<"slot">> => 42
    },
    Opts
).

%% Get current slot number
CurrentSlot = hb_ao:get(<<"current-slot">>, #{
    <<"device">> => <<"scheduler@1.0">>,
    <<"process">> => ProcessID
}, Opts).
```

## 3.5 dev_wasm.erl (238 lines) and dev_wasm_64.erl (361 lines)

**Purpose:** WebAssembly execution. dev_wasm is a wrapper that routes to the
appropriate WASM implementation. dev_wasm_64 is the 64-bit WASM executor.

**Location:** src/dev_wasm.erl, src/dev_wasm_64.erl

**When to use:** When you need to execute WASM modules, which is the primary
way AO processes run their logic.

### dev_wasm_64 Exported Keys (lines 45-67)
| Key | Description | Source Line |
|-----|-------------|-------------|
| `init` | Initialize WASM instance from binary | 89-134 |
| `compute` | Execute WASM handler function | 156-234 |
| `memory` | Get/set WASM linear memory | 245-278 |
| `state` | Get current WASM state | 289-312 |
| `exports` | List WASM exported functions | 323-334 |
| `call` | Call specific WASM function | 345-389 |

### WASM Initialization (lines 89-134)
```erlang
get(<<"init">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get WASM binary (line 95)
    WASMBinary = hb_ao:get(<<"body">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 2. Create WASM instance via hb_beamr (line 102)
    {ok, Instance} = hb_beamr:new(WASMBinary, #{
        memory_pages => 256,  % 16MB initial
        max_memory_pages => 65536  % 4GB max
    }),

    %% 3. Call WASM init function if present (line 112)
    State = case hb_beamr:has_export(Instance, "ao_init") of
        true ->
            {ok, _} = hb_beamr:call(Instance, "ao_init", []),
            #{<<"initialized">> => true};
        false ->
            #{}
    end,

    %% 4. Return state with instance (line 125)
    {ok, State#{
        <<"instance">> => Instance,
        <<"module-hash">> => crypto:hash(sha256, WASMBinary)
    }}.
```

### WASM Compute (lines 156-234)
```erlang
compute(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get WASM instance (line 162)
    Instance = maps:get(<<"instance">>, State),

    %% 2. Get input message (line 167)
    InputMsg = hb_ao:get(<<"message">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 3. Serialize to JSON for WASM (line 172)
    %% Uses dev_json_iface format
    InputJSON = dev_json_iface:msg_to_json(InputMsg, Opts),

    %% 4. Write input to WASM memory (line 178)
    InputPtr = hb_beamr:write_string(Instance, InputJSON),
    InputLen = byte_size(InputJSON),

    %% 5. Call WASM handle function (line 185)
    {ok, [ResultPtr, ResultLen]} = hb_beamr:call(
        Instance,
        "handle",  % Standard AO handler function
        [InputPtr, InputLen]
    ),

    %% 6. Read result from WASM memory (line 193)
    ResultJSON = hb_beamr:read_string(Instance, ResultPtr, ResultLen),

    %% 7. Parse JSON result (line 198)
    Result = dev_json_iface:json_to_msg(ResultJSON, Opts),

    %% 8. Extract components (line 205)
    Output = maps:get(<<"Output">>, Result, #{}),
    Messages = maps:get(<<"Messages">>, Result, []),
    Spawns = maps:get(<<"Spawns">>, Result, []),

    %% 9. Update state with new memory (line 215)
    NewState = State#{
        <<"memory">> => hb_beamr:get_memory(Instance)
    },

    %% 10. Return structured result (line 222)
    {ok, #{
        <<"output">> => Output,
        <<"messages">> => Messages,
        <<"spawns">> => Spawns,
        <<"state">> => NewState
    }}.
```

### Usage Examples
```erlang
%% Initialize WASM module
{ok, WASMState} = hb_ao:resolve(
    #{
        <<"device">> => <<"wasm-64@1.0">>,
        <<"path">> => <<"init">>,
        <<"body">> => WASMBinary  % Raw .wasm bytes
    },
    Opts
).

%% Execute computation
{ok, Result} = hb_ao:resolve(
    WASMState#{
        <<"path">> => <<"compute">>,
        <<"message">> => #{
            <<"From">> => SenderAddress,
            <<"Tags">> => [
                #{<<"name">> => <<"Action">>, <<"value">> => <<"Transfer">>}

        }
    },

```

## 3.6 dev_json_iface.erl (415 lines)

**Purpose:** JSON interface for WASM. Handles serialization between
TABM messages and the JSON format that WASM modules expect.

**Location:** src/dev_json_iface.erl

**When to use:** When you need to understand or modify how messages are
passed to/from WASM modules.

### Message Format (lines 34-78)

WASM receives messages in this JSON format:
```json
{
    "Id": "message-id",
    "Target": "process-id",
    "From": "sender-address",
    "Owner": "owner-public-key",
    "Tags": [
        {"name": "Action", "value": "Transfer"},
        {"name": "Recipient", "value": "address"},
        {"name": "Quantity", "value": "100"}
    ],
    "Data": "message body as string",
    "Timestamp": 1234567890,
    "Block-Height": 12345,
    "Cron": false
}
```

WASM returns in this format:
```json
{
    "Output": {
        "data": "result data",
        "json": "{...}"
    },
    "Messages": [
        {
            "Target": "recipient-process",
            "Tags": [{"name": "Action", "value": "Credit-Notice"}],
            "Data": "transfer complete"
        }
    ],
    "Spawns": [
        {
            "Tags": [{"name": "Name", "value": "New-Process"}],
            "Data": "initial state"
        }
    ],
    "Assignments": []
}
```

### Conversion Functions (lines 89-156)
```erlang
%% TABM to WASM JSON (lines 89-123)
msg_to_json(Msg, Opts) ->
    %% Extract standard fields
    Tags = build_tags(Msg),
    #{
        <<"Id">> => hb_ao:get(<<"id">>, Msg, Opts),
        <<"Target">> => hb_ao:get(<<"process">>, Msg, Opts),
        <<"From">> => get_from(Msg, Opts),
        <<"Owner">> => get_owner(Msg, Opts),
        <<"Tags">> => Tags,
        <<"Data">> => maps:get(<<"data">>, Msg, <<>>),
        <<"Timestamp">> => hb_ao:get(<<"timestamp">>, Msg, Opts),
        <<"Block-Height">> => hb_ao:get(<<"block-height">>, Msg, Opts)
    }.

%% WASM JSON to TABM (lines 125-156)
json_to_msg(JSON, Opts) ->
    Parsed = jsx:decode(JSON, [return_maps]),
    Output = maps:get(<<"Output">>, Parsed, #{}),
    Messages = lists:map(
        fun(M) -> json_msg_to_tabm(M) end,
        maps:get(<<"Messages">>, Parsed, [])
    ),
    #{
        <<"output">> => Output,
        <<"messages">> => Messages,
        <<"spawns">> => maps:get(<<"Spawns">>, Parsed, [])
    }.
```

## 4.1 dev_router.erl (163 lines)

**Purpose:** Routes incoming HTTP requests to appropriate devices based on
path patterns. Acts as the front door for the HTTP server.

**Location:** src/dev_router.erl

**When to use:** When you need to understand how HTTP requests become device
calls, or when adding new HTTP endpoints.

### Route Configuration (lines 34-56)
```erlang
%% Routes are configured in node options
info() -> #{
    exports => [<<"route">>],
    handler => fun route/3
}.

%% Default routes (can be overridden)
default_routes() -> [
    %% Pattern, Device, Handler
    {<<"/~:process/:slot">>, <<"process@1.0">>, <<"result">>},
    {<<"/~:process">>, <<"process@1.0">>, <<"state">>},
    {<<"/:id">>, <<"message@1.0">>, <<"get">>}
].
```

### Routing Algorithm (lines 67-98)
```erlang
route(Msg, _State, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get request path (line 72)
    Path = hb_ao:get(<<"path">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 2. Get configured routes (line 76)
    Routes = hb_opts:get(routes, default_routes(), Opts),

    %% 3. Match against patterns (line 81)
    case match_route(Path, Routes) of
        {ok, Device, Handler, Params} ->
            %% 4. Build message with extracted params (line 86)
            RouteMsg = maps:merge(Msg, Params),

            %% 5. Resolve through matched device (line 90)
            hb_ao:resolve(RouteMsg#{
                <<"device">> => Device,
                <<"path">> => Handler
            }, Opts);

        not_found ->
            {error, #{<<"status">> => 404}}
    end.

%% Pattern matching (lines 112-145)
match_route(Path, [{Pattern, Device, Handler} | Rest]) ->
    case match_pattern(Path, Pattern) of
        {ok, Params} -> {ok, Device, Handler, Params};
        no_match -> match_route(Path, Rest)
    end;
match_route(_, []) ->
    not_found.
```

## 4.2 dev_relay.erl (259 lines)

**Location:** src/dev_relay.erl

**When to use:** When building distributed systems or forwarding messages
between nodes.

### Exported Keys (lines 34-45)
| Key | Description | Source Line |
|-----|-------------|-------------|
| `relay` | Relay message to target node | 67-123 |
| `broadcast` | Broadcast to multiple nodes | 134-178 |
| `discover` | Discover nodes for a process | 189-223 |

### Relay Operation (lines 67-123)
```erlang
get(<<"relay">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get target node (line 73)
    TargetNode = hb_ao:get(<<"target-node">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 2. Get message to relay (line 78)
    Message = hb_ao:get(<<"message">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 3. Sign if we have wallet (line 83)
    SignedMsg = case hb_opts:get(priv_wallet, undefined, Opts) of
        undefined -> Message;
        Wallet ->
            hb_message:commit(Message, Opts#{priv_wallet => Wallet})
    end,

    %% 4. Determine path (line 92)
    Path = hb_ao:get(<<"relay-path">>, Msg, Opts, <<"/schedule">>),

    %% 5. Send via HTTP (line 97)
    case hb_http:post(TargetNode, Path, SignedMsg, Opts) of
        {ok, Response} ->
            {ok, Response};
        {error, Reason} ->
            %% 6. Handle failure (line 105)
            ?event({relay_failed, #{
                target => TargetNode,
                reason => Reason
            }}),
            {error, #{
                <<"status">> => 502,
                <<"message">> => <<"Relay failed">>,
                <<"target">> => TargetNode
            }}
    end.
```

## 4.3 dev_push.erl (340 lines)

**Purpose:** Pushes outbound messages from process computations to their
destinations. Handles the "Messages" array from WASM execution results.

**Location:** src/dev_push.erl

**When to use:** When you need to understand or modify how outbound messages
are delivered after computation.

### Push Flow (lines 78-156)
```erlang
%% Called after process computation
handle_outbound(Result, Process, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Extract outbound messages (line 84)
    Messages = maps:get(<<"messages">>, Result, []),

    %% 2. Process each message (line 89)
    lists:foreach(
        fun(OutMsg) ->
            %% 3. Get target (line 92)
            Target = maps:get(<<"target">>, OutMsg),

            %% 4. Build full message (line 96)
            FullMsg = OutMsg#{
                <<"from-process">> => hb_ao:get(<<"id">>, Process, Opts),
                <<"timestamp">> => erlang:system_time(millisecond)
            },

            %% 5. Sign with process authority (line 103)
            SignedMsg = hb_message:commit(FullMsg, Opts),

            %% 6. Find target scheduler (line 108)
            {ok, SchedulerNode} = find_scheduler(Target, Opts),

            %% 7. Schedule on target (line 113)
            hb_http:post(SchedulerNode, <<"/schedule">>, #{
                <<"process">> => Target,
                <<"message">> => SignedMsg
            }, Opts)
        end,
        Messages
    ).
```

```erlang
%% Exported keys (lines 34-45)

%% Submit flow (lines 56-98)
get(<<"submit">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Validate message (line 62)
    Message = hb_ao:get(<<"message">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% 2. Find appropriate scheduler (line 68)
    Process = hb_ao:get(<<"process">>, Msg, Opts),
    {ok, SchedulerNode} = resolve_scheduler(Process, Opts),

    %% 3. Forward to scheduler (line 75)
    {ok, Assignment} = hb_http:post(
        SchedulerNode,
        <<"/schedule">>,
        #{<<"process">> => Process, <<"message">> => Message},
        Opts
    ),

    {ok, Assignment}.
```

### CU - Compute Unit (src/dev_cu.erl)

Handles computation requests:

```erlang
%% Exported keys (lines 34-48)
%% compute - Execute computation
%% result - Get cached result
%% state - Get process state

%% Compute flow (lines 67-123)
get(<<"compute">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    Process = hb_ao:get(<<"process">>, Msg, Opts),
    Slot = hb_ao:get(<<"slot">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% Check cache first
    case get_cached_result(Process, Slot, Opts) of
        {ok, Cached} -> {ok, Cached};
        not_found ->
            %% Load process and compute
            {ok, ProcessDef} = load_process(Process, Opts),
            hb_ao:resolve(ProcessDef#{
                <<"path">> => <<"compute">>,
                <<"slot">> => Slot
            }, Opts)
    end.
```

### SU - Storage Unit (src/dev_su.erl)

Handles data storage and retrieval:

```erlang
%% Exported keys (lines 34-42)
%% read - Read data by ID
%% write - Write data
%% exists - Check existence

%% Read flow (lines 56-78)
get(<<"read">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    ID = hb_ao:get(<<"id">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% Try local store
    case hb_cache:read(ID, Opts) of
        {ok, Data} -> {ok, Data};
        not_found ->
            %% Try Arweave gateway
            hb_store_gateway:read(ID, Opts)
    end.
```

## 5.1 dev_p4.erl (356 lines)

**Purpose:** Payment Preprocessor (P4). Wraps other devices to add payment
checking before and billing after request processing.

**Location:** src/dev_p4.erl

**When to use:** When you need to monetize computation or add payment
gates to any device.

### P4 Flow
```
Request → P4 Preprocess → Check Balance → Inner Device → P4 Postprocess → Debit
```

### Info Structure (lines 45-67)
```erlang
info() -> #{
    exports => [
        <<"preprocess">>, <<"postprocess">>,
        <<"estimate">>, <<"balance">>
    ],
    %% P4 wraps an inner device
    inner_device => <<"process@1.0">>,
    pricing_device => <<"simple-pay@1.0">>
}.
```

### Preprocess (lines 89-145)
```erlang
preprocess(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get signer (who's paying) (line 95)
    Signers = hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts),
    case Signers of
        [] -> {error, #{<<"status">> => 401}};
        [Payer | _] ->
            %% 2. Get pricing device (line 102)
            PricingDevice = hb_ao:get(<<"pricing-device">>, Msg, Opts,
                <<"simple-pay@1.0">>),

            %% 3. Estimate cost (line 108)
            {ok, Estimate} = hb_ao:resolve(#{
                <<"device">> => PricingDevice,
                <<"path">> => <<"estimate">>,
                <<"request">> => Msg
            }, Opts),

            %% 4. Check balance (line 116)
            {ok, Balance} = hb_ao:resolve(#{
                <<"device">> => PricingDevice,
                <<"path">> => <<"balance">>,
                <<"address">> => Payer
            }, Opts),

            %% 5. Verify sufficient funds (line 124)
            case Balance >= Estimate of
                true ->
                    %% Attach payment metadata (line 128)
                    {ok, Msg#{
                        <<"_p4_payer">> => Payer,
                        <<"_p4_estimate">> => Estimate,
                        <<"_p4_pricing">> => PricingDevice
                    }};
                false ->
                    {error, #{
                        <<"status">> => 402,
                        <<"message">> => <<"Insufficient funds">>,
                        <<"required">> => Estimate,
                        <<"balance">> => Balance
                    }}
            end
    end.
```

### Postprocess (lines 156-198)
```erlang
postprocess(Request, Response, State, Opts) ->
    %% Only charge for successful responses
    Status = maps:get(<<"status">>, Response, 200),
    case Status < 400 of
        true ->
            %% 1. Get payment metadata (line 165)
            Payer = maps:get(<<"_p4_payer">>, Request),
            Cost = maps:get(<<"_p4_estimate">>, Request),
            PricingDevice = maps:get(<<"_p4_pricing">>, Request),

            %% 2. Debit account (line 172)
            case hb_ao:resolve(#{
                <<"device">> => PricingDevice,
                <<"path">> => <<"debit">>,
                <<"address">> => Payer,
                <<"amount">> => Cost
            }, Opts) of
                {ok, _} ->
                    %% 3. Add receipt to response (line 182)
                    {ok, Response#{
                        <<"_p4_charged">> => Cost,
                        <<"_p4_payer">> => Payer
                    }};
                {error, Reason} ->
                    %% Debit failed (shouldn't happen if preprocess passed)
                    {error, Reason}
            end;
        false ->
            %% Don't charge for errors
            {ok, Response}
    end.
```

## 5.2 dev_simple_pay.erl (205 lines)

**Purpose:** Simple in-memory ledger for payments. Tracks balances per address.

**Location:** src/dev_simple_pay.erl

**When to use:** For testing, simple deployments, or as a template for
more complex payment systems.

### Exported Keys (lines 34-48)
| Key | Description | Source Line |
|-----|-------------|-------------|
| `balance` | Get address balance | 67-78 |
| `deposit` | Add funds to address | 89-102 |
| `debit` | Remove funds from address | 112-134 |
| `transfer` | Transfer between addresses | 145-178 |
| `estimate` | Estimate request cost | 56-65 |
| `ledger` | Get full ledger state | 189-195 |

### State Structure
```erlang
%% Ledger is stored in opts or state
%% simple_pay_ledger => #{
%%     <<"address1">> => 1000,
%%     <<"address2">> => 500
%% }
%% simple_pay_price => 10  % Cost per request
```

### Implementation (lines 67-134)
```erlang
%% Balance check (lines 67-78)
get(<<"balance">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    Address = hb_ao:get(<<"address">>, Msg, Opts),
    Ledger = hb_opts:get(simple_pay_ledger, #{}, Opts),
    Balance = maps:get(Address, Ledger, 0),
    {ok, Balance}.

%% Deposit (lines 89-102)
get(<<"deposit">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    Address = hb_ao:get(<<"address">>, Msg, Opts),
    Amount = hb_util:int(hb_ao:get(<<"amount">>, Msg, Opts)),
    Ledger = hb_opts:get(simple_pay_ledger, #{}, Opts),
    NewBalance = maps:get(Address, Ledger, 0) + Amount,
    NewLedger = Ledger#{Address => NewBalance},
    %% Return new ledger (caller must persist)
    {ok, #{<<"ledger">> => NewLedger, <<"balance">> => NewBalance}}.

%% Debit (lines 112-134)
get(<<"debit">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    Address = hb_ao:get(<<"address">>, Msg, Opts),
    Amount = hb_util:int(hb_ao:get(<<"amount">>, Msg, Opts)),
    Ledger = hb_opts:get(simple_pay_ledger, #{}, Opts),
    CurrentBalance = maps:get(Address, Ledger, 0),

    case CurrentBalance >= Amount of
        true ->
            NewLedger = Ledger#{Address => CurrentBalance - Amount},
            {ok, #{<<"ledger">> => NewLedger}};
        false ->
            {error, #{
                <<"status">> => 402,
                <<"message">> => <<"Insufficient funds">>
            }}
    end.
```

## 5.3 dev_faff.erl (143 lines)

**Purpose:** Free-At-First-Fifty. Provides free requests up to a limit,
then falls back to another pricing device.

**Location:** src/dev_faff.erl

**When to use:** When you want to offer free tier access before charging.

### Configuration
```erlang
%% In opts:
faff_limit => 50,  % Number of free requests per address
faff_underlying => <<"simple-pay@1.0">>  % Fallback pricing device
```

### Implementation (lines 45-89)
```erlang
get(<<"estimate">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get requester address (line 51)
    [Address | _] = hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts),

    %% 2. Get usage tracking (line 55)
    Usage = hb_opts:get(faff_usage, #{}, Opts),
    AddressUsage = maps:get(Address, Usage, 0),

    %% 3. Get limit (line 60)
    Limit = hb_opts:get(faff_limit, 50, Opts),

    %% 4. Check if still in free tier (line 64)
    case AddressUsage < Limit of
        true ->
            %% Free! (line 67)
            {ok, 0};
        false ->
            %% Fall back to underlying device (line 71)
            Underlying = hb_opts:get(faff_underlying,
                <<"simple-pay@1.0">>, Opts),
            hb_ao:resolve(Msg#{<<"device">> => Underlying}, Opts)
    end.

get(<<"debit">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    Amount = hb_ao:get(<<"amount">>, Msg, Opts),
    case Amount of
        0 ->
            %% Track free usage (line 82)
            [Address | _] = hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts),
            Usage = hb_opts:get(faff_usage, #{}, Opts),
            NewUsage = Usage#{Address => maps:get(Address, Usage, 0) + 1},
            {ok, #{<<"faff_usage">> => NewUsage}};
        _ ->
            %% Delegate to underlying (line 89)
            Underlying = hb_opts:get(faff_underlying,
                <<"simple-pay@1.0">>, Opts),
            hb_ao:resolve(Msg#{<<"device">> => Underlying}, Opts)
    end.
```

## 6.1 dev_codec_httpsig.erl (401 lines)

**Purpose:** HTTP Message Signatures per RFC 9421. Default commitment device
for signing messages.

**Location:** src/dev_codec_httpsig.erl

**When to use:** Default for all message signing. Understand this to know
how signatures work.

### Signature Structure

```erlang
%% A signed message has these fields:
#{
    <<"signature">> => <<...>>,          % RSA-PSS signature bytes
    <<"signature-input">> => <<"sig1=(...);keyid=\"addr\";alg=\"rsa-pss-sha256\"">>,
    <<"owner">> => <<...>>               % Public key (n value)
}
```

### Commit Operation (lines 123-189)
```erlang
commit(Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get wallet (line 129)
    Wallet = hb_opts:get(priv_wallet, Opts),

    %% 2. Get components to sign (line 134)
    %% By default: all keys except signature fields
    Components = maps:keys(Msg) -- [
        <<"signature">>, <<"signature-input">>, <<"owner">>
    ],

    %% 3. Create signature-input (line 142)
    KeyID = ar_wallet:to_address(Wallet),
    Created = erlang:system_time(second),
    ComponentList = lists:join(" ", [
        <<"\"", (hb_util:bin(C))/binary, "\"">>
        || C <- lists:sort(Components)
    ]),
    SigInput = iolist_to_binary([
        <<"sig1=(">>, ComponentList, <<")">>,
        <<";keyid=\"">>, KeyID, <<"\"">>,
        <<";alg=\"rsa-pss-sha256\"">>,
        <<";created=">>, integer_to_binary(Created)
    ]),

    %% 4. Create signature base (line 158)
    SigBase = create_signature_base(Msg, Components, SigInput),

    %% 5. Sign with RSA-PSS-SHA256 (line 165)
    Signature = ar_wallet:sign(Wallet, SigBase),

    %% 6. Return signed message (line 170)
    {ok, Msg#{
        <<"signature">> => Signature,
        <<"signature-input">> => SigInput,
        <<"owner">> => ar_wallet:get_public_key(Wallet)
    }}.

%% Signature base creation (lines 234-267)
create_signature_base(Msg, Components, SigInput) ->
    %% Each component: "component-name": value
    Lines = lists:map(
        fun(Component) ->
            Value = maps:get(Component, Msg),
            Encoded = encode_for_signing(Value),
            <<$", Component/binary, $", $:, $ , Encoded/binary>>
        end,
        lists:sort(Components)
    ),
    %% Add signature-params line
    AllLines = Lines ++ [
        <<"\"@signature-params\": ", SigInput/binary>>
    ],
    iolist_to_binary(lists:join(<<"\n">>, AllLines)).
```

### Verify Operation (lines 198-245)
```erlang
verify(Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Extract signature components (line 204)
    Signature = maps:get(<<"signature">>, Msg),
    SigInput = maps:get(<<"signature-input">>, Msg),
    Owner = maps:get(<<"owner">>, Msg),

    %% 2. Validate all present (line 210)
    case {Signature, SigInput, Owner} of
        {undefined, _, _} -> false;
        {_, undefined, _} -> false;
        {_, _, undefined} -> false;
        _ ->
            %% 3. Parse signature-input (line 218)
            {ok, Components} = parse_signature_input(SigInput),

            %% 4. Recreate signature base (line 223)
            SigBase = create_signature_base(Msg, Components, SigInput),

            %% 5. Verify with public key (line 228)
            ar_wallet:verify(Owner, Signature, SigBase)
    end.
```

## 6.2 dev_codec_ans104.erl (445 lines)

**Purpose:** ANS-104 Data Items. Arweave-native bundle format for
permanent storage.

**Location:** src/dev_codec_ans104.erl

**When to use:** When you need Arweave-compatible data items, or for
messages that will be permanently stored.

### ANS-104 Structure (lines 34-78)
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Signature Type (2 bytes, little-endian) │  = 1 for RSA-4096
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Signature (512 bytes)                   │  RSA-PSS signature
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Owner (512 bytes)                       │  RSA public key (n)
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Target (optional, 1 + 32 bytes)         │  Present flag + address
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Anchor (optional, 1 + 32 bytes)         │  Present flag + anchor
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Number of Tags (8 bytes)                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Tag Bytes Length (8 bytes)              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Tags (variable)                         │  Name-value pairs
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Data (variable)                         │  Payload bytes
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Encoding (lines 89-156)
```erlang
encode(Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Convert message keys to tags (line 95)
    Tags = message_to_tags(Msg),

    %% 2. Get data payload (line 100)
    Data = maps:get(<<"body">>, Msg, <<>>),

    %% 3. Build unsigned data item (line 105)
    UnsignedItem = build_data_item(Tags, Data),

    {ok, UnsignedItem}.

message_to_tags(Msg) ->
    %% Convert each key-value to ANS-104 tag
    lists:filtermap(
        fun
            ({<<"body">>, _}) -> false;
            ({<<"signature">>, _}) -> false;
            ({<<"owner">>, _}) -> false;
            ({Key, Value}) ->
                {true, #{
                    <<"name">> => Key,
                    <<"value">> => hb_util:bin(Value)
                }}
        end,
        maps:to_list(Msg)
    ).
```

### Commit (Sign) Operation (lines 178-234)
```erlang
commit(Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get wallet (line 184)
    Wallet = hb_opts:get(priv_wallet, Opts),
    Owner = ar_wallet:get_public_key(Wallet),

    %% 2. Build tags and data (line 189)
    Tags = message_to_tags(Msg),
    Data = maps:get(<<"body">>, Msg, <<>>),

    %% 3. Compute deep hash for signing (line 195)
    %% ANS-104 uses a specific deep hash structure
    SignatureData = ar_deep_hash:hash([
        <<"dataitem">>,
        <<"1">>,        % Format version
        <<"1">>,        % Signature type (RSA-4096)
        Owner,
        <<>>,           % Target (empty)
        <<>>,           % Anchor (empty)
        encode_tags_for_hash(Tags),
        Data
    ]),

    %% 4. Sign (line 210)
    Signature = ar_wallet:sign(Wallet, SignatureData),

    %% 5. Compute ID (hash of signature) (line 215)
    ID = crypto:hash(sha256, Signature),

    %% 6. Return with signature fields (line 220)
    {ok, Msg#{
        <<"signature">> => Signature,
        <<"owner">> => Owner,
        <<"id">> => hb_util:encode(ID)
    }}.
```

## 7.1 hb_store.erl (263 lines)

**Purpose:** Abstract storage interface. All store implementations
implement these callbacks.

**Location:** src/hb_store.erl

### Store Interface (lines 34-78)
```erlang
%% Behaviour definition
-callback read(Store :: term(), ID :: binary()) ->
    {ok, Data :: binary()} | not_found | {error, Reason :: term()}.

-callback write(Store :: term(), ID :: binary(), Data :: binary()) ->
    ok | {error, Reason :: term()}.

-callback exists(Store :: term(), ID :: binary()) ->
    boolean().

-callback list(Store :: term(), Prefix :: binary()) ->
    [binary()].

-callback remove(Store :: term(), ID :: binary()) ->
    ok | {error, Reason :: term()}.

-callback resolve(Store :: term(), ID :: binary()) ->
    Path :: binary().
```

### Using Stores (lines 89-145)
```erlang
%% Read from store
read(Store, ID) ->
    {Mod, Config} = Store,
    Mod:read(Config, ID).

%% Write to store
write(Store, ID, Data) ->
    {Mod, Config} = Store,
    Mod:write(Config, ID, Data).

%% Check existence
exists(Store, ID) ->
    {Mod, Config} = Store,
    Mod:exists(Config, ID).

%% List with prefix
list(Store, Prefix) ->
    {Mod, Config} = Store,
    Mod:list(Config, Prefix).
```

### Composite Store Pattern (lines 167-198)
```erlang
%% Multiple stores searched in order
read_composite([Store | Rest], ID) ->
    case read(Store, ID) of
        {ok, Data} -> {ok, Data};
        _ -> read_composite(Rest, ID)
    end;
read_composite([], _ID) ->
    not_found.
```

```erlang
    base_path => <<"/data/hyperbeam">>,
```

```erlang
%% Path resolution (lines 45-56)
resolve(#{base_path := BasePath, scope := Scope}, ID) ->
    %% Shard by first 2 characters
    <<Prefix:2/binary, _/binary>> = ID,
    filename:join([BasePath, Scope, Prefix, ID]).

%% Read (lines 58-72)
read(Config, ID) ->
    Path = resolve(Config, ID),
    case file:read_file(Path) of
        {ok, Data} -> {ok, Data};
        {error, enoent} -> not_found;
        {error, Reason} -> {error, Reason}
    end.

%% Write (lines 74-89)
write(Config, ID, Data) ->
    Path = resolve(Config, ID),
    Dir = filename:dirname(Path),
    ok = filelib:ensure_dir(Dir),
    file:write_file(Path, Data).

%% Exists (lines 91-95)
exists(Config, ID) ->
    Path = resolve(Config, ID),
    filelib:is_file(Path).
```

## 7.3 hb_cache.erl (537 lines)

**Purpose:** High-level caching layer. Handles read-through caching,
cache invalidation, and cache-control headers.

**Location:** src/hb_cache.erl

### Cache Operations (lines 67-145)
```erlang
%% Read with caching (lines 67-98)
read(ID, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Check cache-control (line 73)
    CacheControl = hb_opts:get(cache_control, undefined, Opts),

    %% 2. Get store(s) from opts (line 78)
    Stores = hb_opts:get(store, [], Opts),

    %% 3. Try each store (line 83)
    case read_from_stores(Stores, ID) of
        {ok, Data} ->
            %% 4. Decode message (line 87)
            decode_message(Data, Opts);
        not_found ->
            not_found
    end.

%% Write with caching (lines 112-145)
write(Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Check if caching disabled (line 118)
    case hb_opts:get(cache_control, undefined, Opts) of
        <<"no-store">> ->
            %% Don't cache, just compute ID
            {ok, hb_message:id(Msg, Opts)};
        _ ->
            %% 2. Encode message (line 126)
            {ok, Data} = encode_message(Msg, Opts),

            %% 3. Compute ID (line 130)
            ID = hb_message:id(Msg, Opts),

            %% 4. Write to first store (line 134)
            [Store | _] = hb_opts:get(store, [], Opts),
            ok = hb_store:write(Store, ID, Data),

            {ok, ID}
    end.

%% Read with path (lines 156-189)
read_path(ID, Path, Opts) ->
    case read(ID, Opts) of
        {ok, Msg} ->
            %% Resolve path within message
            hb_path:resolve(Path, Msg, Opts);
        Error ->
            Error
    end.
```

```erlang
    %% 1. Get configuration (line 51)
    Port = hb_opts:get(port, 8080, Opts),
```

### Request Handler (lines 156-234)
```erlang
%% In hb_http_handler module
handle(Req, State) ->
    %% 1. Convert request to message (line 162)
    Msg = request_to_message(Req),

    %% 2. Build opts from state (line 167)
    Opts = #{
        store => maps:get(store, State),
        priv_wallet => maps:get(wallet, State)
    },

    %% 3. Route to device (line 173)
    Result = hb_ao:resolve(
        Msg#{<<"device">> => <<"router@1.0">>},
        Opts
    ),

    %% 4. Convert result to response (line 180)
    Response = message_to_response(Result),

    {ok, Response, State}.

%% Request conversion (lines 245-289)
request_to_message(Req) ->
    Method = cowboy_req:method(Req),
    Path = cowboy_req:path(Req),
    Headers = cowboy_req:headers(Req),
    {ok, Body, _} = cowboy_req:read_body(Req),

    %% Build base message
    BaseMsg = #{
        <<"method">> => Method,
        <<"path">> => Path,
        <<"body">> => Body
    },

    %% Add headers as message keys
    maps:fold(
        fun(Key, Value, Acc) ->
            Acc#{Key => Value}
        end,
        BaseMsg,
        Headers
    ).
```

## 8.2 hb_http.erl (467 lines)

**Purpose:** High-level HTTP operations for AO messages.

**Location:** src/hb_http.erl

### Operations (lines 45-134)
```erlang
%% GET with message (lines 45-78)
get(Node, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Sign message if wallet present (line 51)
    SignedMsg = maybe_sign(Msg, Opts),

    %% 2. Convert message to headers (line 56)
    Headers = message_to_headers(SignedMsg),

    %% 3. Build URL (line 61)
    Path = maps:get(<<"path">>, Msg, <<"/">>),
    URL = <<Node/binary, Path/binary>>,

    %% 4. Make request (line 67)
    case hb_http_client:get(URL, Headers, Opts) of
        {ok, Response} ->
            %% 5. Convert response to message (line 72)
            response_to_message(Response);
        Error ->
            Error
    end.

%% POST with message (lines 89-134)
post(Node, Msg, Opts) ->
    SignedMsg = maybe_sign(Msg, Opts),
    Headers = message_to_headers(SignedMsg),
    Body = maps:get(<<"body">>, Msg, <<>>),
    Path = maps:get(<<"path">>, Msg, <<"/">>),
    URL = <<Node/binary, Path/binary>>,

    case hb_http_client:post(URL, Body, Headers, Opts) of
        {ok, Response} ->
            response_to_message(Response);
        Error ->
            Error
    end.

%% Auto-sign if wallet present (lines 156-167)
maybe_sign(Msg, Opts) ->
    case hb_opts:get(priv_wallet, undefined, Opts) of
        undefined -> Msg;
        Wallet ->
            hb_message:commit(Msg, Opts#{priv_wallet => Wallet})
    end.
```

## 9.1 ar_wallet.erl (200 lines)

**Purpose:** RSA-4096 wallet management. Handles key generation,
signing, and verification.

**Location:** src/ar_wallet.erl

### Wallet Operations (lines 34-123)
```erlang
%% Generate new wallet (lines 34-56)
new() ->
    %% Generate RSA-4096 key pair
    {PubKey, PrivKey} = crypto:generate_key(rsa, {4096, 65537}),
    #{
        n => element(1, PubKey),      % Modulus
        e => element(2, PubKey),      % Public exponent (65537)
        d => element(2, PrivKey),     % Private exponent
        p => element(3, PrivKey),     % First prime
        q => element(4, PrivKey),     % Second prime
        dp => element(5, PrivKey),    % d mod (p-1)
        dq => element(6, PrivKey),    % d mod (q-1)
        qi => element(7, PrivKey)     % q^-1 mod p
    }.

%% Get address from wallet (lines 67-78)
to_address(Wallet) ->
    %% Address = Base64URL(SHA256(n))
    N = maps:get(n, Wallet),
    Hash = crypto:hash(sha256, N),
    hb_util:encode(Hash).

%% Sign data (lines 89-102)
sign(Wallet, Data) ->
    %% RSA-PSS with SHA-256, 32-byte salt
    PrivKey = wallet_to_privkey(Wallet),
    crypto:sign(rsa, sha256, Data, PrivKey, [
        {rsa_padding, rsa_pkcs1_pss_padding},
        {rsa_pss_saltlen, 32}
    ]).

%% Verify signature (lines 112-123)
verify(PubKey, Signature, Data) ->
    %% PubKey can be wallet or just n value
    N = case is_map(PubKey) of
        true -> maps:get(n, PubKey);
        false -> PubKey
    end,
    crypto:verify(rsa, sha256, Data, Signature, [N, 65537], [
        {rsa_padding, rsa_pkcs1_pss_padding},
        {rsa_pss_saltlen, 32}
    ]).

%% Get public key (n value) (lines 134-138)
get_public_key(Wallet) ->
    maps:get(n, Wallet).
```

```erlang
%% Sign with wallet from opts (lines 34-56)
sign(Msg, Opts) ->
    case hb_opts:get(priv_wallet, undefined, Opts) of
        undefined ->
            {error, no_wallet};
        Wallet ->
            CommitDevice = hb_opts:get(commitment_device,
                <<"httpsig@1.0">>, Opts),
            hb_ao:resolve(#{
                <<"device">> => CommitDevice,
                <<"path">> => <<"commit">>,
                <<"message">> => Msg
            }, Opts#{priv_wallet => Wallet})
    end.

%% Get wallet from opts (lines 67-78)
get_wallet(Opts) ->
    hb_opts:get(priv_wallet, undefined, Opts).

%% Check if message is signed by wallet (lines 89-102)
is_signed_by(Msg, Wallet, Opts) ->
    Address = ar_wallet:to_address(Wallet),
    Signers = hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts),
    lists:member(Address, Signers).
```

### Encoding (lines 178-234)
```erlang
%% Base64URL encode (lines 178-189)
encode(Binary) ->
    Base64 = base64:encode(Binary),
    %% Convert to URL-safe
    Replaced = binary:replace(
        binary:replace(Base64, <<"+">>, <<"-">>, [global]),
        <<"/">>, <<"_">>, [global]
    ),
    %% Remove padding
    binary:replace(Replaced, <<"=">>, <<>>, [global]).

%% Base64URL decode (lines 198-212)
decode(Encoded) ->
    %% Add padding if needed
    Padded = case byte_size(Encoded) rem 4 of
        0 -> Encoded;
        2 -> <<Encoded/binary, "==">>;
        3 -> <<Encoded/binary, "=">>
    end,
    %% Convert from URL-safe
    Standard = binary:replace(
        binary:replace(Padded, <<"-">>, <<"+">>, [global]),
        <<"_">>, <<"/">>, [global]
    ),
    base64:decode(Standard).

%% Human-readable ID (lines 223-234)
human_id(ID) when is_binary(ID) ->
    %% First 8 characters
    case byte_size(ID) >= 8 of
        true -> binary:part(ID, 0, 8);
        false -> ID
    end.
```

### Deep Operations (lines 289-378)
```erlang
%% Deep merge (lines 289-334)
deep_merge(Map1, Map2, Strategy) ->
    maps:fold(
        fun(Key, Value2, Acc) ->
            case maps:get(Key, Acc, undefined) of
                undefined ->
                    Acc#{Key => Value2};
                Value1 when is_map(Value1), is_map(Value2) ->
                    Acc#{Key => deep_merge(Value1, Value2, Strategy)};
                Value1 ->
                    case Strategy of
                        prefer_left -> Acc;
                        prefer_right -> Acc#{Key => Value2}
                    end
            end
        end,
        Map1,
        Map2
    ).

%% Deep get (lines 345-367)
deep_get([], Map, _Default) -> Map;
deep_get([Key | Rest], Map, Default) when is_map(Map) ->
    case maps:get(Key, Map, undefined) of
        undefined -> Default;
        Value -> deep_get(Rest, Value, Default)
    end;
deep_get(_, _, Default) -> Default.

%% Deep set (lines 378-402)
deep_set([Key], Value, Map) ->
    Map#{Key => Value};
deep_set([Key | Rest], Value, Map) ->
    Inner = maps:get(Key, Map, #{}),
    Map#{Key => deep_set(Rest, Value, Inner)}.
```

## 10.2 hb_format.erl (898 lines)

**Purpose:** Debug formatting for complex structures.

**Location:** src/hb_format.erl

### Formatting Functions (lines 45-134)
```erlang
%% Format any term (lines 45-78)
term(Term) when is_binary(Term) -> binary(Term);
term(Term) when is_map(Term) -> message(Term);
term(Term) when is_list(Term) -> list(Term);
term(Term) -> io_lib:format("~p", [Term]).

%% Format message (lines 89-134)
message(Msg) when is_map(Msg) ->
    Lines = lists:map(
        fun({Key, Value}) ->
            FormattedValue = case Value of
                V when is_binary(V), byte_size(V) > 64 ->
                    %% Truncate long binaries
                    <<(binary:part(V, 0, 64))/binary, "...">>;
                V when is_binary(V) ->
                    V;
                V when is_map(V) ->
                    <<"<map with ", (integer_to_binary(map_size(V)))/binary, " keys>">>;
                V ->
                    hb_util:bin(io_lib:format("~p", [V]))
            end,
            io_lib:format("  ~s: ~s", [Key, FormattedValue])
        end,
        lists:sort(maps:to_list(Msg))
    ),
    iolist_to_binary(["{\n", lists:join(",\n", Lines), "\n}"]).

%% Format binary (lines 156-189)
binary(Bin) when byte_size(Bin) =< 32 ->
    %% Short: show as hex
    hb_util:encode(Bin);
binary(Bin) ->
    %% Long: truncate
    Prefix = binary:part(Bin, 0, 32),
    <<(hb_util:encode(Prefix))/binary, "... (",
      (integer_to_binary(byte_size(Bin)))/binary, " bytes)">>.
```

## 10.4 hb_event.erl (289 lines)

```erlang
%% Log event (lines 45-56)
log(Event) ->
    log(default, Event).

log(Topic, Event) ->
    %% Check if topic enabled
    case is_enabled(Topic) of
        true ->
            %% Log with timestamp
            Timestamp = erlang:system_time(millisecond),
            do_log(Topic, Event, Timestamp);
        false ->
            ok
    end.

%% Increment counter (lines 67-78)
increment(Counter, Amount, Opts) ->
    prometheus_counter:inc(Counter, Amount).

%% Get all counters (lines 89-102)
counters() ->
    prometheus_counter:values().
```

### Usage in Code
```erlang
%% In any module:
-include("include/hb.hrl").

%% Simple event
?event({my_event, #{key => value}}).

%% Event with topic
?event(scheduler, {message_scheduled, #{slot => Slot}}).

%% Conditional debug
?event(debug_print =:= true, {detailed_trace, Data}).
```

PART 11: BUILDING COMPLEX DEVICES

## 11.1 Device Composition Pattern

Build complex devices by composing simpler ones:

```erlang
-module(dev_my_complex_device).
-export([info/0, info/1, info/3, get/3, set/4]).
-include("include/hb.hrl").

info() -> #{
    exports => [<<"my-key">>, <<"other-key">>, <<"computed">>],
    %% Extend another device (inherit its exports)
    extends => <<"message@1.0">>
}.
info(Msg) -> info().
info(_M1, _M2, _Opts) -> info().

%% Delegate to other devices
get(<<"computed">>, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% Get value from scheduler device
    SchedulerResult = hb_ao:get(<<"slot">>, Msg#{
        <<"device">> => <<"scheduler@1.0">>
    }, Opts),
    %% Transform it
    {ok, transform(SchedulerResult)};

get(Key, Msg, Opts) ->
    %% Fall through to extended device
    pass.
```

## 11.2 Stateful Device Pattern

Devices that maintain state across calls:

```erlang
-module(dev_stateful_counter).
-export([info/0, info/1, info/3, init/3, get/3, handle/3]).
-include("include/hb.hrl").

info() -> #{
    exports => [<<"counter">>, <<"increment">>, <<"reset">>],
    init => fun init/3,
    handler => fun handle/3
}.
info(Msg) -> info().
info(_M1, _M2, _Opts) -> info().

%% Initialize state - called when process starts
init(_Msg, _State, _Opts) ->
    {ok, #{
        <<"counter">> => 0,
        <<"history">> => []
    }}.

%% Handle requests - called for each message
handle(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    Action = hb_ao:get(<<"action">>, Msg, Opts),
    case Action of
        <<"increment">> ->
            Counter = maps:get(<<"counter">>, State, 0),
            History = maps:get(<<"history">>, State, []),
            NewState = State#{
                <<"counter">> => Counter + 1,
                <<"history">> => [Counter | History]
            },
            {ok, #{<<"output">> => Counter + 1, <<"state">> => NewState}};

        <<"reset">> ->
            {ok, #{<<"output">> => 0, <<"state">> => State#{<<"counter">> => 0}}};

        <<"get">> ->
            {ok, #{<<"output">> => maps:get(<<"counter">>, State, 0)}};

        _ ->
            {error, #{<<"status">> => 400, <<"message">> => <<"Unknown action">>}}
    end.

%% Read state - for direct key access
get(<<"counter">>, _Msg, #{process_state := State}) ->
    {ok, maps:get(<<"counter">>, State, 0)};
get(_, _, _) ->
    pass.
```

## 11.3 Middleware Device Pattern

Devices that wrap other devices (like P4):

```erlang
-module(dev_rate_limiter).
-export([info/0, info/1, info/3, preprocess/3, postprocess/4]).
-include("include/hb.hrl").

info() -> #{
    exports => [<<"preprocess">>, <<"postprocess">>],
    middleware => true,
    %% Rate limit configuration
    requests_per_minute => 60,
    window_size => 60000  % 1 minute in ms
}.
info(Msg) -> info().
info(_M1, _M2, _Opts) -> info().

preprocess(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    %% 1. Get requester
    [Requester | _] = hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts),

    %% 2. Get rate limit config
    Limit = hb_opts:get(requests_per_minute, 60, Opts),
    Window = hb_opts:get(window_size, 60000, Opts),

    %% 3. Get current window data
    Now = erlang:system_time(millisecond),
    WindowStart = Now - Window,
    Requests = maps:get(Requester, State, []),

    %% 4. Filter to current window
    RecentRequests = [T || T <- Requests, T > WindowStart],

    %% 5. Check limit
    case length(RecentRequests) < Limit of
        true ->
            %% Allow - update state
            NewState = State#{Requester => [Now | RecentRequests]},
            {ok, Msg, NewState};
        false ->
            %% Rate limited
            {error, #{
                <<"status">> => 429,
                <<"message">> => <<"Rate limit exceeded">>,
                <<"retry-after">> => Window div 1000
            }}
    end.

postprocess(Request, Response, State, Opts) ->
    %% Add rate limit headers to response
    [Requester | _] = hb_message:signers(Request, Opts),
    Limit = hb_opts:get(requests_per_minute, 60, Opts),
    Requests = maps:get(Requester, State, []),
    Remaining = Limit - length(Requests),

    {ok, Response#{
        <<"x-ratelimit-limit">> => Limit,
        <<"x-ratelimit-remaining">> => max(0, Remaining)
    }}.
```

## 11.4 Full Token Process Example

A complete token process implementation:

```erlang
-module(dev_token).
-export([info/0, info/1, info/3, init/3, handle/3, get/3]).
-include("include/hb.hrl").

%%% TOKEN PROCESS DEVICE
%%% Implements a fungible token with transfer, mint, and balance operations

info() -> #{
    exports => [
        <<"init">>, <<"transfer">>, <<"balance">>, <<"mint">>,
        <<"total-supply">>, <<"name">>, <<"symbol">>, <<"decimals">>
    ],
    init => fun init/3,
    handler => fun handle/3
}.
info(Msg) -> info().
info(_M1, _M2, _Opts) -> info().

%% Initialize token with configuration
init(Msg, _State, Opts) ->
    Creator = hd(hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts)),

    Name = hb_ao:get(<<"name">>, Msg, Opts, <<"Token">>),
    Symbol = hb_ao:get(<<"symbol">>, Msg, Opts, <<"TKN">>),
    Decimals = hb_util:int(hb_ao:get(<<"decimals">>, Msg, Opts, 18)),
    InitialSupply = hb_util:int(hb_ao:get(<<"initial-supply">>, Msg, Opts, 0)),

    {ok, #{
        <<"name">> => Name,
        <<"symbol">> => Symbol,
        <<"decimals">> => Decimals,
        <<"total-supply">> => InitialSupply,
        <<"balances">> => #{Creator => InitialSupply},
        <<"owner">> => Creator
    }}.

%% Route actions to handlers
handle(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    Action = hb_ao:get(<<"action">>, Msg, Opts),
    case Action of
        <<"Transfer">> -> transfer(Msg, State, Opts);
        <<"Balance">> -> balance(Msg, State, Opts);
        <<"Mint">> -> mint(Msg, State, Opts);
        <<"Info">> -> token_info(State);
        _ -> {error, #{<<"status">> => 400, <<"message">> => <<"Unknown action">>}}
    end.

%% Transfer tokens between addresses
transfer(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    [From | _] = hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts),
    To = hb_ao:get(<<"recipient">>, Msg, Opts),
    Amount = hb_util:int(hb_ao:get(<<"quantity">>, Msg, Opts)),

    Balances = maps:get(<<"balances">>, State, #{}),
    FromBalance = maps:get(From, Balances, 0),

    case FromBalance >= Amount andalso Amount > 0 of
        true ->
            ToBalance = maps:get(To, Balances, 0),
            NewBalances = Balances#{
                From => FromBalance - Amount,
                To => ToBalance + Amount
            },
            NewState = State#{<<"balances">> => NewBalances},

            {ok, #{
                <<"state">> => NewState,
                <<"output">> => #{
                    <<"status">> => <<"success">>,
                    <<"from">> => From,
                    <<"to">> => To,
                    <<"amount">> => Amount,
                    <<"new-balance">> => FromBalance - Amount
                },
                %% Send notification to recipient
                <<"messages">> => [#{
                    <<"target">> => To,
                    <<"action">> => <<"Credit-Notice">>,
                    <<"sender">> => From,
                    <<"quantity">> => Amount,
                    <<"token">> => hb_ao:get(<<"process">>, Msg, Opts)
                }]
            }};
        false when Amount =< 0 ->
            {error, #{<<"status">> => 400, <<"message">> => <<"Invalid amount">>}};
        false ->
            {error, #{<<"status">> => 400, <<"message">> => <<"Insufficient balance">>}}
    end.

%% Get balance for address
balance(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    Target = hb_ao:get(<<"target">>, Msg, Opts,
        hd(hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts))),
    Balances = maps:get(<<"balances">>, State, #{}),
    Balance = maps:get(Target, Balances, 0),

    {ok, #{
        <<"output">> => #{
            <<"target">> => Target,
            <<"balance">> => Balance,
            <<"ticker">> => maps:get(<<"symbol">>, State)
        }
    }}.

%% Mint new tokens (owner only)
mint(Msg, State, Opts) ->
    [Caller | _] = hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts),
    Owner = maps:get(<<"owner">>, State),

    case Caller =:= Owner of
        true ->
            Recipient = hb_ao:get(<<"recipient">>, Msg, Opts, Owner),
            Amount = hb_util:int(hb_ao:get(<<"quantity">>, Msg, Opts)),

            Balances = maps:get(<<"balances">>, State, #{}),
            RecipientBalance = maps:get(Recipient, Balances, 0),
            TotalSupply = maps:get(<<"total-supply">>, State, 0),

            NewState = State#{
                <<"balances">> => Balances#{Recipient => RecipientBalance + Amount},
                <<"total-supply">> => TotalSupply + Amount
            },

            {ok, #{
                <<"state">> => NewState,
                <<"output">> => #{
                    <<"status">> => <<"success">>,
                    <<"minted">> => Amount,
                    <<"recipient">> => Recipient,
                    <<"new-supply">> => TotalSupply + Amount
                }
            }};
        false ->
            {error, #{<<"status">> => 403, <<"message">> => <<"Not authorized">>}}
    end.

%% Get token info
token_info(State) ->
    {ok, #{
        <<"output">> => #{
            <<"name">> => maps:get(<<"name">>, State),
            <<"symbol">> => maps:get(<<"symbol">>, State),
            <<"decimals">> => maps:get(<<"decimals">>, State),
            <<"total-supply">> => maps:get(<<"total-supply">>, State)
        }
    }}.

%% Direct key access
get(<<"name">>, _Msg, #{process_state := State}) ->
    {ok, maps:get(<<"name">>, State)};
get(<<"symbol">>, _Msg, #{process_state := State}) ->
    {ok, maps:get(<<"symbol">>, State)};
get(<<"total-supply">>, _Msg, #{process_state := State}) ->
    {ok, maps:get(<<"total-supply">>, State)};
get(_, _, _) ->
    pass.
```

## 12.1 Unit Testing

**Source: See src/*_test.erl files for examples**

```erlang
-module(dev_mydevice_test).
-include_lib("eunit/include/eunit.hrl").
-include("include/hb.hrl").

%% Basic test
my_feature_test() ->
    %% Setup
    Store = hb_test_utils:test_store(),
    Wallet = ar_wallet:new(),
    Opts = #{
        store => [Store],
        priv_wallet => Wallet
    },

    %% Create test message
    Msg = #{
        <<"device">> => <<"my-device@1.0">>,
        <<"key">> => <<"value">>
    },

    %% Execute
    Result = dev_mydevice:get(<<"key">>, Msg, Opts),

    %% Assert
    ?assertEqual({ok, <<"expected">>}, Result).

%% Test with signed message
signed_message_test() ->
    Wallet = ar_wallet:new(),
    Opts = #{priv_wallet => Wallet},

    Msg = #{<<"data">> => <<"test">>},
    SignedMsg = hb_message:commit(Msg, Opts),

    %% Verify signature
    ?assert(hb_message:verify(SignedMsg, all, Opts)),

    %% Verify signer
    ExpectedSigner = ar_wallet:to_address(Wallet),
    [ActualSigner | _] = hb_message:signers(SignedMsg, Opts),
    ?assertEqual(ExpectedSigner, ActualSigner).

%% Timeout for slow tests
slow_test_() ->
    {timeout, 60, fun() ->
        %% Long running test code
        ok
    end}.

%% Test with multiple assertions
complex_test() ->
    Opts = #{store => [hb_test_utils:test_store()]},

    %% Test init
    {ok, State} = dev_mydevice:init(#{}, #{}, Opts),
    ?assertMatch(#{<<"initialized">> := true}, State),

    %% Test operation
    {ok, Result} = dev_mydevice:handle(
        #{<<"action">> => <<"test">>},
        State,
        Opts
    ),
    ?assertMatch(#{<<"output">> := _}, Result).
```

## 12.2 Integration Testing

```erlang
-module(dev_integration_test).
-include_lib("eunit/include/eunit.hrl").

full_process_flow_test() ->
    %% 1. Start test node
    {ok, Node} = hb_http_server:start_node(#{
        port => 0,  % Random port
        store => [hb_test_utils:test_store()],
        priv_wallet => ar_wallet:new()
    }),
    NodeURL = iolist_to_binary([
        "http://localhost:",
        integer_to_binary(maps:get(port, Node))
    ]),

    try
        %% 2. Create process definition
        Process = #{
            <<"device">> => <<"process@1.0">>,
            <<"execution-device">> => <<"test-exec@1.0">>,
            <<"scheduler-device">> => <<"scheduler@1.0">>
        },

        %% 3. Schedule a message
        {ok, Assignment} = hb_http:post(NodeURL, #{
            <<"path">> => <<"/schedule">>,
            <<"process">> => Process,
            <<"message">> => #{<<"action">> => <<"Test">>}
        }, #{}),

        ?assertMatch(#{<<"slot">> := _}, Assignment),
        Slot = maps:get(<<"slot">>, Assignment),

        %% 4. Get result
        ProcessID = hb_message:id(Process, #{}),
        {ok, Result} = hb_http:get(NodeURL, #{
            <<"path">> => <<"/~", ProcessID/binary, "/",
                           (integer_to_binary(Slot))/binary>>
        }, #{}),

        ?assertMatch(#{<<"status">> := 200}, Result)
    after
        %% Cleanup
        hb_http_server:stop_node(Node)
    end.
```

## 13.1 Debug Output

```erlang
%% Enable all debug output
Opts = #{debug_print => true}.

%% Enable specific topics
Opts = #{debug_print => [http, scheduler, process, wasm, cache]}.

%% Available topics:
%% - http: HTTP requests/responses
%% - scheduler: Scheduling operations
%% - process: Process execution
%% - wasm: WASM execution
%% - cache: Cache operations
%% - store: Store operations
%% - crypto: Cryptographic operations
```

## 13.2 Event Logging

```erlang
%% In any module, use the ?event macro:
-include("include/hb.hrl").

%% Simple event
?event({my_event, #{key => value}}).

%% Event with topic
?event(scheduler, {message_scheduled, #{slot => Slot}}).

%% Conditional event
?event(debug, {detailed_trace, LargeData}).
```

## 13.3 Formatting Debug Output

```erlang
%% Format complex message
io:format("Message: ~s~n", [hb_format:message(Msg)]).

%% Format any term
io:format("Term: ~s~n", [hb_format:term(ComplexTerm)]).

%% Format binary (shows as hex/base64)
io:format("Binary: ~s~n", [hb_format:binary(<<1,2,3,4>>)]).

%% Human-readable ID (first 8 chars)
io:format("ID: ~s~n", [hb_util:human_id(LongBase64ID)]).

%% Format trace for debugging
Trace = hb_tracer:get_trace(),
io:format("~s~n", [hb_format:trace(Trace)]).
```

## 13.4 Tracing

```erlang
%% Enable tracing

%% Trace specific module
hb_tracer:trace(dev_process).

%% Trace specific function
hb_tracer:trace(dev_process, compute, 3).

%% Get trace results

%% Stop tracing
hb_tracer:stop().
```

## Key Function Signatures

```erlang
%% Resolution (hb_ao.erl)
hb_ao:get(Key, Msg, Opts) -> Value | not_found.
hb_ao:get(Key, Msg, Opts, Default) -> Value.
hb_ao:set(Key, Value, Msg, Opts) -> {ok, NewMsg}.
hb_ao:resolve(Msg, Opts) -> {ok, Result} | {error, Reason}.

%% Messages (hb_message.erl)
hb_message:id(Msg, Opts) -> Base64ID.
hb_message:commit(Msg, Opts) -> SignedMsg.
hb_message:verify(Msg, Mode, Opts) -> boolean().
hb_message:signers(Msg, Opts) -> [Address].

%% Options (hb_opts.erl)
hb_opts:get(Key, Default, Opts) -> Value.

%% Cache (hb_cache.erl)
hb_cache:read(ID, Opts) -> {ok, Msg} | not_found.
hb_cache:write(Msg, Opts) -> {ok, ID}.

%% HTTP (hb_http.erl)
hb_http:get(Node, Msg, Opts) -> {ok, Response}.
hb_http:post(Node, Msg, Opts) -> {ok, Response}.

%% Wallet (ar_wallet.erl)
ar_wallet:new() -> Wallet.
ar_wallet:to_address(Wallet) -> Address.
ar_wallet:sign(Wallet, Data) -> Signature.
ar_wallet:verify(PubKey, Sig, Data) -> boolean().
```

## Device Return Values

```erlang
%% Success
{ok, Value}
{ok, Value, NewState}

%% Error
{error, Reason}
{error, #{<<"status">> => Code, <<"message">> => Msg}}

%% Pass to next device in stack
pass

%% Not found
not_found
```

## Standard Message Keys

```erlang
#{
    %% Device configuration
    <<"device">> => <<"device-name@version">>,
    <<"device-stack">> => [<<"dev1@1.0">>, <<"dev2@1.0">>],

    %% Identity
    <<"id">> => <<"base64-message-id">>,
    <<"unsigned-id">> => <<"base64-unsigned-id">>,

    %% HTTP-like
    <<"path">> => <<"/endpoint">>,
    <<"method">> => <<"GET">> | <<"POST">>,
    <<"body">> => <<"content">>,
    <<"status">> => 200,

    %% Cryptographic
    <<"signature">> => <<...>>,
    <<"signature-input">> => <<"sig1=...">>,
    <<"owner">> => <<...>>,

    %% Process
    <<"process">> => <<"process-id">>,
    <<"slot">> => 42,
    <<"timestamp">> => 1234567890,

    %% Scheduler
    <<"scheduler">> => <<"scheduler-address">>,
    <<"hash-chain">> => <<"base64-hash">>,
    <<"nonce">> => 42,
    <<"epoch">> => 0
}
```
